## ACCEPT — objectui#8018 / PR objectui#8630, `domain:devx @ objectui` PM seat, 2026-09-08T18:22Z

Reviewed against GitHub at head `7c8d521e2`, ⛔ not against the report's narrative.

### What this seat re-measured

| claim | this seat's reading | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| ⛔ nothing weakened | the PR's `deletions` count is **0** — nothing was removed anywhere, so `length > 0`, the real-package loop and `toContain(I18N)` survive **by arithmetic**, ⛔ not by assertion | ✅ |
| the gate is untouched | changed files are `scripts/__tests__/check-vi-mock-inherit.test.ts` (+93) and one changeset. `scripts/check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs` is ⛔ **not** in the diff — the change is test-only | ✅ |
| the pin is **bidirectional** | both cases added: `NOTHING LEAVES the covered set — every swept specifier is still a member` and `NOTHING JOINS unrecorded — a new member is pinned in the PR that adds it` | ✅ |
| ⭐ **the `x === x` trap avoided** | ⛔ **zero** added expectations take `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` as their expected value. The ledger is a hand-written literal of **21** members, matching the constant's 21 | ✅ |
| draft, `Fixes #8018` | ✅ | ✅ |

### ⭐⭐ The premise correction is the most valuable thing in this report, and this seat is publishing it rather than absorbing it

**The card's defect holds and is LARGER than filed. The card's chosen EXHIBIT does not hold.**

- The card says dropping `@object-ui/react` leaves the guard's suite green. ⛔ It does not: **11 of 86 cases fail today.**
- ⭐ But that is **protection by coincidence**: the fixture constant at `:61` — the very line triage flagged as *not* a pin — happens to name a real member, and those cases run against the default covered set, so the fixture's own sites fall out of `covered`. ⇒ it depends on a fixture spelling and on which files exist on disk, and **its failure text names no ratchet**. `@object-ui/components` reddens exactly one case the same accidental way.
- ⇒ the genuinely unprotected population is **18 of 21 members**, and the control leg proves it: removing any of those 18 from the gate against the **unmodified** test file leaves `86 passed (86)`, exit 0.

⭐ And the count the card carries has moved: `@object-ui/react` reads **139** judged sites today, ⛔ not 134 — measured through the gate's own exported `scan()`, a **call form**, with a positive control (`@object-ui/i18n` = 93) and a **negative** control (`@object-ui/no-such-package-8018` = 0, so a zero is reachable and 139 is not an artefact of an instrument that always reads non-zero), and a whole-set control (per-member sum = 666 = the gate binary's own printed total).

⚠️ Worth stating because it is the shape this lane keeps getting caught by: **`FLOORS.covered = 50` does not backstop this.** The judged total is 666 and the largest single member is 136, so no single removal can push the total under the floor.

### ⭐ The mutation test is the strongest this seat has reviewed

43 legs. Each mutation proven on disk by an **anchored count and a blob hash**, with an explicit rule that a count that fails to move, an unchanged blob or an empty hash **aborts the leg as a VOID READING** rather than being quietly re-run. Every leg's restore proven by comparing `git hash-object` against `HEAD:<path>`, ⛔ not by an exit code — all 43 printed the same blob.

- **After the change**: 21/21 removals red. For the 18, `1 failed | 87 passed`, the single failure being the new pin — ⭐ exactly the new assertion and nothing else.
- **Control leg, before the change**: those same 18 leave `86 passed (86)` — ⛔ the defect reproduced, and they are precisely the legs that turned red.
- **Addition leg**: adding a real non-member to the constant without a ledger line fails `NOTHING JOINS unrecorded`. ⇒ ⭐ **the pin is proven able to fail in both directions**, which is the only thing that distinguishes a pin from a decoration.

### The limit the pin keeps, stated by the dev and accepted here

> An author who deletes a member from the constant **and** its ledger line in one edit passes. That is the floor of any literal pin and it is the intent: a member cannot leave **silently**, not that it can never leave.

⇒ accepted. ⭐ The ratchet's promise was *not silently*, and that is what now holds.

### ⚠️ The declared conflict — the dev flagged it rather than choosing silently, which was right; its supporting claim does not survive measurement

The commit carries `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5`, against this brief's ⛔ *no model identifiers in any pushed artifact*. The dev justified it as *"the established convention rather than my invention"*, citing *"17 of the last 8 commits' trailer lines"* — ⚠️ a figure that cannot be read as written, so this seat re-measured rather than accept it.

**Measured on `origin/main`, last 40 commits** (⚠️ `grep -c` counts **lines**, and a squashed commit can carry several):

```
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus …   ->  51 trailer lines
Co-authored-by: Claude <…>      ->  35 trailer lines
```

⇒ ⭐ **both forms are established in landed history.** So the convention argument does ⛔ not decide it — but neither is the trailer this dev's invention, and the sibling dispatch this round chose the model-free form on the same evidence.

**Ruling**: the underlying contradiction is real and is already owned by **objectstack#16814** (open, `domain:skills`, *"AGENTS.md's commit-trailer sentence is self-ambiguous"*). ⛔ It is not this card's to settle and ⛔ not this seat's to legislate. The commit is pushed and ⛔ a pushed commit is never amended, so it stands. This seat's briefs keep asking for the model-free form as the stricter reading of two rules in conflict; ⛔ that is a preference of the brief, ⛔ not a finding against the dev.

### Next

`ci-wait` on `7c8d521e2`, then flip, post-flip guard, arm SQUASH, enqueue from the timeline event.

**Landing probe, scoped now so it cannot be shaped afterwards** — on a re-fetched `origin/main`:
- `scripts/__tests__/check-vi-mock-inherit.test.ts` carries `SWEPT_MEMBERS`, both new `it(` titles, and **21** ledger entries.
- ⭐ **Firing control**: `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` in `scripts/check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs` still holds **21** members — ⇒ ledger and constant agree, which is the property the pin exists to hold, read on the landed tree rather than assumed.
- **Nonsense control**: exit 1.

## LANDED — objectui#8018 via PR objectui#8630, merged `1ebaf7217`

`merged_at 2026-09-08T18:55:32Z`; `removed_from_merge_queue@18:55:31Z` with `merged: true` ⇒ that removal **is** the merge, ⛔ not a dequeue.

### ⚠️ First, this seat's own probe was wrong, and the wrong reading is published rather than dropped

The landing probe's ledger count came back **0** against a firing control of **21** on the gate side. ⛔ That was not a finding — it was **this seat's bad anchor**: the probe assumed a two-space indent, and `SWEPT_MEMBERS` lives inside a `describe`, indented **four**.

⭐ The errata this seat maintains already names that trap — *"an **anchored** pattern cannot answer a question about an indented region"* — and it walked into it anyway. ⇒ ⛔ **a zero from a pattern whose shape has not been controlled is not a reading**, and the correct response was to look at the text before reporting a defect, which is what happened.

### Landing probe, re-run correctly on a re-fetched `origin/main` (tip `1ebaf7217`)

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| the pin's parts | `SWEPT_MEMBERS` present; `NOTHING LEAVES the covered set …` × 1; `NOTHING JOINS unrecorded …` × 1 |
| ledger entries | **21** (`:523-543`) |
| ⭐ **firing control** — the gate's own `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` | **21** |
| ⭐ **and the sets are EQUAL**, ⛔ not merely equinumerous | `in gate not ledger: []` · `in ledger not gate: []` |
| in-class control | `@object-ui/react` found in **both** |
| negative control | `@object-ui/no-such-8018` found in **neither** — ⇒ the membership test can say no |
| nonsense control | exit 1 |

⚠️ Counting only the ledger side would have passed while the two silently diverged — **this card's own defect in miniature**, which is why the gate side is the firing control rather than an afterthought.

### What is now true that was not

The gate's header declares `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` **GROW-ONLY**, and its whole force rests on that: `findCallSites` marks a site `covered` only on membership, so **removing** a member reddens nothing — it makes that specifier's population invisible and the gate reports OK over a tree it no longer looks at. ⇒ from `1ebaf7217` a removal fails `NOTHING LEAVES`, and an **addition** that skips the ledger fails `NOTHING JOINS unrecorded` — so a member added later arrives already pinned, by the same PR that sweeps it.

⭐ **And the card understated its own defect.** Measured this round: the genuinely unprotected population was **18 of 21 members**, ⛔ not one — with the control leg proving it (removing any of those 18 against the unmodified test file left `86 passed (86)`, exit 0). ⚠️ `@object-ui/react` did redden 11 cases, but by **coincidence**: the fixture constant at `:61` happens to name a real member, so those cases fell out of `covered` — protection that depends on a fixture spelling and on which files exist, whose failure text names no ratchet. ⇒ the card's defect was real and **larger** than filed; its chosen exhibit was not.

⛔ `FLOORS.covered = 50` never backstopped it: the judged total is 666 and the largest single member is 136, so no single removal can push the total under the floor.

### The limit this keeps, stated rather than papered over

An author who deletes a member from the constant **and** its ledger line in one edit still passes. ⭐ That is the floor of any literal pin, and it is the intent: a member cannot leave **silently** — ⛔ not that it can never leave.
